newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson Breweries settles Coors dispute.
newsitem.headline: Molson Breweries settles Coors dispute.

text.p: Canadian brewer Molson Breweries said on Wednesday that it has settled a dispute with U.S. beermaker Adolph Coors Co in their battle over Molson's licensing rights to Coors' top-selling beers in Canada.
Under the agreement, Molson paid Coors C$100 million and will take a C$32.5 million after-tax charge against fiscal 1997 earnings, the company said in a statement.
Molson said it also agreed to form a new partnership with Coors and Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd to manage Coors brands in Canada.
Last October, an arbitration panel tore up Molson's contract for Coors Light and Original Coors, which accounted for eight percent of the Canadian brewer's sales volume.
The panel said Molson breached its licensing deal by allowing Miller Brewing Co to buy a 20 percent stake in the Canadian brewer in 1993 without Coors consent.
Molson Breweries continued to brew and sell Coors beers in Canada under an interim agreement until the dispute was settled.
Miller Brewing is a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc. Molson Breweries is also owned 40 percent each by Foster's Brewing Group and Toronto-based Molson Cos Ltd.

"We are delighted to be able to put our legal issues behind us. We look upon this as a long-term relationship between parties that know and enjoy the beer business and who have shown in recent months that they can work well together to continue Coors Light's growth as the number one light beer in Canada," Molson and Coors said in a joint statement.
Molson, Coors and Foster's have also entered into a conditional agreement to form a partnership to manage Coors brands in Canada.
The proposed partnership will be owned 50.1 percent by Coors and 24.95 percent each by Molson and Foster's.

The partnership is structured to be a long-term relationship with both sides having the option to terminate, without cause, on two years notice. Under the agreement, Molson Breweries will manufacture, distribute and sell all beer for the partnership.
The partnership and brewing agreement is subject to regulatory approval and approval from Miller Brewing before December 31, 1997.
Pending Miller's approval, Molson Breweries and Coors have agreed that Molson Breweries will continue to brew and market Coors product for an interim period through December 31, 1997.
If Miller does not give its approval, all Molson Breweries' arrangements with Coors will terminate no later than June 15, 1998, the statement said.

Molson Breweries said the C$100 million payment is "full settlement of the arbitration and all other legal proceedings between Coors and Molson Breweries and its partners, Molson, Foster's and Miller Brewing Company."
"The after-tax effect to Molson, of this settlement, is estimated to be C$32.5 million. This amount, plus related other costs, will be charged against fiscal 1997 earnings," the statement said.
